newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Kohl reaffirm euro confidence.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Kohl reaffirm euro confidence.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl reiterated their determination to launch a single European currency on time in 1999 in talks in Bonn on Wednesday, a French official source said on Thursday.

The same message came from Bonn, where government spokesman Peter Hausmann said that, in addition to their traditional joint message of confidence in monetary union, the leaders agreed to work closely together to prepare a European Union summit on institutional reform in June.
"They emphasised their total determination to launch the euro (single currency) at the scheduled date," the French official said.
Despite lingering doubts about Germany's ability to meet the fitness test for monetary union, Kohl's decision to stand for re-election next year has renewed optimism in the project.

Kohl and Chirac, who met in Bonn on Wednesday evening for informal talks, agreed to get together several times ahead of a June summit in Amsterdam on the reform of EU institutions, the French official said.

Despite the two countries' leading role in pushing for the creation of a single currency, France and Germany will have to overcome differences on EU reform to prevent its institutions becoming unwieldy as the 15-nation bloc expands membership.

Diplomats and officials say France has been pushing hard for a reduction in the number of commissioners which each member country can have appointed to the top European Commission posts, while Germany wants to avoid the wrath of smaller member states which could lose out from such a move.
